construct: Alcohol dehydrogenase oxidizes methanol toward toxic formic acid/formate. Formate accumulation produces a high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and disrupts mitochondrial respiration; retinal and optic-nerve tissues are particularly vulnerable. Fomepizole limits toxicity by inhibiting alcohol dehydrogenase before toxic metabolites accumulate.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Windshield-washer-fluid ingestion followed by visual symptoms, a high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and an osmolar gap identifies methanol poisoning with formate toxicity.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Oxalic acid is the strongest toxic-alcohol distractor, but it is generated from ethylene glycol and is associated with calcium oxalate deposition and kidney injury rather than characteristic retinal toxicity.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The exposure and visual toxicity uniquely identify formic acid/formate as the toxic metabolite.
